decision: Not selected for production. Exact-interval UPDATE removes verified SQL/WAL work and improves fresh requests, but the primary GC-aged comparison fails performance acceptance. Later timing diagnostics do not consistently reproduce the overwrite stalls and retain a severe small-file WAL-fsync/journal wait. The cause of the variant/timing interaction remains unresolved.

diagnostic_before.scope: Foreground 4 KiB FUSE overwrite diagnosis; only 512 requests are instrumented, fsync is separately timed. Two balanced orders, fresh and GC-aged workspaces. Per-thread wall/CPU scopes and SQLite VM/syscall counts are diagnostic, not adoption throughput.

diagnostic_after.scope: Foreground 4 KiB FUSE overwrite diagnosis; only 512 requests are instrumented, fsync is separately timed. Two balanced orders, fresh and GC-aged workspaces. Per-thread wall/CPU scopes and SQLite VM/syscall counts are diagnostic, not adoption throughput.

timeline.scope: Separate instrumented FUSE diagnosis. Same aged workload and preparation as the plain comparison; slow syscalls and checkpoint/sync timeline plus 10 ms owned-thread samples. Not adoption throughput.

plain_tails.scope: Separate plain-binary FUSE diagnosis with external 10 ms owned-thread samples. Same aged workload/preparation, no in-process hooks. Separate window; not pooled into the primary comparison.

diagnostic_before.scope: Host-wide, includes preparation and cleanup. No attribution to any other workload.

diagnostic_after.scope: Host-wide, includes preparation and cleanup. No attribution to any other workload.

fuse.scope: Host-wide, includes preparation and cleanup. No attribution to any other workload.

timeline.scope: Host-wide, includes preparation and cleanup. No attribution to any other workload.

validation.skip_reason: Experimental format 1004 has no production-v1 migration

limitations: Instrumented timing includes wall/CPU timers and is diagnostic only; FUSE throughput uses separate plain binaries.
VM steps count wrapped sqlite3_step calls. sqlite3_exec internal steps are not counted; compare cached and updated only.
WAL byte counts are bytes accepted by write syscalls, not physical device writes.
FUSE uses one foreground callback thread plus a checkpoint worker; counters are per-thread.
Fsync is separate from random-write request time; phase medians cannot be added to reconstruct a median total.
Shared host, warm caches, local ext4, fsync durability, small sample; no device-level cause is established.
No owned builds or correctness tests overlap measurement, and no global cache or kernel changes are made.
The optimization also applies conceptually to BLOB version tables; this experiment changes only format-1004 copies.
Production installation and storage format remain unchanged. No remote backend, production migration or online backup protocol.
All slow samples remain in the report; previous comparison windows are not pooled into this one.
Detailed dbstat page-layout tables and complete request/event/wait traces are retained in local raw artifacts, identified by the manifest.
Kernel wait sampling identifies where time is spent, not the device-level cause; separate diagnostic windows do not override the primary acceptance failure.
